# Journey to becoming a clinical bioinformatician
## Where I want to be in 1-2 years
In one to two years I want to work as a junior clinical bioinformatician or a NGS molecular diagnostics specialist at a hospital or research institute analysing RNA seq and clinical data to answer questions about ....

## Where I stand now

To see where my skills compare with what employers ask for, I analysed 17 vacancies (11 in the Netherlands and 6 abroad) for (junior) bio-informaticians and noted which skills each one requires

```{r vacancy-table}
library(tidyverse)
Vacancy_skillset <- tibble(
  skills = c("Python", "R", "Bash/Linux", "Git", "Statistics/ML", "Snakemake/Nextflow", "Dockers/Containers", "NGS data analysis and file formats (fastq, bam"),
  frequency_in_vacancies = c(5, 3, 7, 1, 2, 9, 1, 8),
  Do_I_have_it = c("Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "Partly", "No", "No", "Basic"))

Vacancy_skillset
ggplot(Vacancy_skillset, aes(x = reorder(skills, frequency_in_vacancies), y = frequency_in_vacancies, fill = Do_I_have_it)) + 
  geom_col() + 
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "List of skills asked for in clinical bio-informatics vacancies",
       x = "Skills",
       y = "Number of vacancies") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Current Strenghts
On the data side I work in R (RNA-seq analysis, metagenomics, GO enrichment), Python and Bash, and I use Git and RMarkdown for reproducible reporting. On the lab side I have hands-on experience with SDS-PAGE, Western blot, BCA assays, PCR and sterile technique, which helps me understand how the data I analyse is produced

### Vacancies information
Most vacancies in that have a requirement for data science in research, biotech, diagnostics ask for knowledge in python, R and statistics/machine learning and experience with snakemake or Nextflow. For example a vacancy in Amsterdam UMC (genome diagnostics) asks for Python, familiarity with quality assurance systems and ISO standards, and willingness to work with Linux and HPC while a UMC Groningen vacancy asks for experience with Snakemake or Nextflow plus knowledge of data stewardship rules, Erasmus MC asks for Python or Java and Nextflow or Snakemake, and Maastricht UMC+ lists HPC, Linux, SLURM and Snakemake/Nextflow.

## What I still want to learn
Out of the 17 vacancies most ask for experience in snakemake and nextflow. However for this course I will be tackling machine learning/statistics and using that on NGS data analysis. I chose machine learning first I am curious about what expression data can predict, and it builds on the R/Python skills I already have

# Learning machine learning for biology: predicting cancer type from RNA-seq data

## Why this skill

<!-- Short justification that links back to the previous chapter. -->
In my vacancy analysis, statistics and machine learning were requested in several vacancies and are only partly covered by my current skills. I apply the skill to a biological question: **can machine learning distinguish cancer types (or subtypes) based on gene expression profiles?**

## Plan (32 hours)

| Step | Hours | When | Result |
|:-----|------:|:-----|:-------|
| Choosing the skill and justification | 2 | 17–22 Nov | Chapter above |
| Planning | 2 | 17–22 Nov | This section |
| Learning: ML basics and a tutorial in **[scikit-learn / tidymodels]** | 8 | 23 Nov – 6 Dec | Practice notebook on tutorial data |
| Applying: models on a new RNA-seq dataset | 14 | 7–20 Dec | Analysis with trained and evaluated models |
| Write-up | 6 | 21–27 Dec | Final chapter on this portfolio |
| Buffer | – | 28 Dec – 2 Jan | Corrections before the 3 January deadline |

**What I need:** a public RNA-seq dataset with cancer-type labels from **[source, e.g. TCGA or GEO]**, **[Python with scikit-learn or R with tidymodels]**, and a tutorial or course on supervised learning.

## How I will show I learned the skill

- A reproducible analysis (Rmd or notebook, with code in a GitHub repository).
- Data preparation and a proper **train/test split**
- At least two models
- Evaluation with a PCR matrix, plus the most important genes and whether they make biological sense.
- A reflection on limitations: many more genes than samples, overfitting, and what the model can and cannot say.
